Hi Alyssa — great to meet you on the call. Appreciate the sample. Below is a concise post-call recap and proposed next steps so we can align the POC scope.

Recap / immediate recommendations:
1) Model candidates (balanced accuracy + safety):
   - redwood/econ-7b-rlhf: strong recall on intent classification; fast inference for baseline triage.
   - redwood/rlhf-13b-q4 (quantized 4-bit): good middle ground for cost/accuracy when using prefix caching for common dialog turns.
   - open-llama-30b-refined: higher accuracy on subtle clinical language, but heavier infra; use as a fallback for high-risk cases.

2) Safety & refusal evaluation plan:
   - We'll run the sample set you provided through our refusal/safety prompt suite (attached: safety_eval_promptset.jsonl) which includes guardrail prompts for suicidal ideation, medication instructions, and PHI handling.
   - We'll classify outcomes as: Acceptable, Safe Refusal, Risky Acceptance, or Ambiguous.
   - Provide a triaged list of example failures and recommended prompt-level mitigations (explicit refusal templates, fallback routing).

3) Metrics & benchmarks:
   - Primary metrics: refusal precision on sensitive cases, false-refusal rate on benign clinical instructions, intent classification F1.
   - We will run small benchmarks (per-model) and share a Drive folder with result summaries and token cost estimates.

4) Proposed timeline / mutual action plan:
   - Today: Redwood ingests your sample and confirms formats. (We received HS_clinical_samples.csv)
   - 48–72 hours: initial safety eval runs on 3 model candidates + summary report.
   - Week 2: follow-up call to review failure modes and confirm POC config (routing/quantization).

Attachments: safety_eval_promptset.jsonl, HS_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.docx

Next steps for you: confirm POI (scope = triage transcripts only?) and any regulatory constraints (e.g., state-specific MD guidance) we should encode in rules. Also confirm an initial contact for legal/security questions so we can pre-stage SOC2 artifacts if needed.

I'll loop Rafael for infra sizing and Marcus for evaluation metrics validation.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Adding a couple technical notes on infra/config that will matter for the POC and the safety evals: 

- For throughput and cost efficiency, we recommend running the quantized 4-bit variants for the initial pass (redwood/rlhf-13b-q4). Quantization keeps token cost low while preserving most refusal behavior we see in our benchmarks.
- Use a two-tier routing policy: cheap baseline model for classification + a higher-capability model (open-llama-30b-refined or redwood/econ-7b-rlhf fallback) for flagged high-risk cases. This reduces false negatives on critical misclassifications.
- Potential quality regression risk: when we apply aggressive prompt-level guardrails (e.g., forced refusal templates), there can be an increased false-refusal rate on ambiguous but benign clinical guidance. We'll track false-refusal rate closely and recommend fine-grained prompt tuning rather than broad-spectrum rules where possible.
- I'll kick off the eval runs against the 3 candidate models (batch runs) and upload results to the Drive folder I created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarkFolder

I'll estimate we'll have the first consolidated results (safety classification + token cost estimates) in ~72 hours.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
